#  14489 - English for Life Sciences Modulübersicht  
|  Module Number:   | **14489**  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Module Title:  | **English for Life Sciences**  |  
|  Englisch für Biowissenschaften   |  
| Department:  |  ZES - Language Centre   |  
| Responsible Staff Member:  | 
  * Klug, Kristina 

 |  
| Language of Teaching / Examination:  | English  |  
| Duration:  | 1 semester  |  
| Frequency of Offer:  |  Every summer semester   |  
| Credits:  |  
| Learning Outcome:  | In this module, participants will improve their language skills in the following areas: · **Enhanced Communication Skills** : Develop the ability to effectively communicate complex scientific and healthcare concepts in English. · **Technical Vocabulary** : Gain proficiency in the specialized vocabulary and terminology used in life sciences and healthcare. · **Critical Reading and Analysis** : Improve skills in reading and critically analysing scientific texts, research papers, and healthcare documents. · **Presentation Skills** : Learn to create and deliver clear, concise, and engaging presentations on scientific and healthcare topics. · **Cultural Competence** : Understand the importance of cultural sensitivity and effective communication in diverse professional settings.  |  
| Contents:  | · **Terminology** : Understanding and using specialized vocabulary related to life sciences and healthcare (e.g. equations, macromolecules). · **Scientific Communication** : Techniques for effectively communicating scientific information, including summarizing research papers and presenting findings (e.g. lab rules, set up of experiments, preventing harm). · **Cultural Sensitivity** : Learning to communicate effectively with colleagues from diverse cultural backgrounds. · **Ethical Considerations** : Discussing ethical issues in life sciences & healthcare and how to communicate them. · **Case Studies** : Analyzing real-life case studies to apply communication skills in practical scenarios (e.g. BCIs, gene editing, mRNA vaccinations). · **Reading skills:** selecting texts and information, identifying purpose and audience, skimming vs. scanning, identifying relationships between ideas and theories, comparing fact vs opinion.   |  
| Recommended Prerequisites:  | English knowledge: Abitur / CEFR level B1+  |  
| Mandatory Prerequisites:  | none  |  
| Forms of Teaching and Proportion:  | 
  * Exercise / 4 Hours per Week per Semester 
  * Self organised studies / 120 Hours 

 |  
| Teaching Materials and Literature:  | Armer: Cambridge English for Scientists. CUP, 2017.Evans, Dooley Norton: Genetic Engineering. Express Publishing, 2021.Delta Academic Objectives: Reading Skills; Louis Rogers (2017) Cambridge: Study Reading 2nd Ed.; Eric H. Glendinning (2013) University of Michigan Press: English for Nursing, Academic Skills; Bosher (2015) Brock Biology of Microorganisms by Madigan, M.T., Martinko J.M. & Parker, J., International Edition, Tenth Edition, Pearson 2003 Language and grammar books General and specialised dictionaries Articles of specific journals’ websites  |  
| Module Examination:  | Continuous Assessment (MCA)  |  
| Assessment Mode for Module Examination:  |  Continuous assessment 1 test to check understanding of scientific papers (15%) 20min 1 test to check listening comprehension (15%) 20min 1 Presentation of 20min (70%)  |  
| Evaluation of Module Examination:  | Performance Verification – graded  |  
| Limited Number of Participants:  | None  |
